# Wiki CLI Contract Requirements Checklist: Self-Improving Architecture

**Purpose**: Test whether the agent-shaped command requirements (FR-027–FR-039, US7, SC-010) and contracts/wiki-cli.md are complete, unambiguous, consistent, and measurable.
**Created**: 2026-09-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [research.md](../research.md) · [data-model.md](../data-model.md) · [contracts/](../contracts/) · [quickstart.md](../quickstart.md) (branch `030-self-improving-architecture` @ 5dbd8e83, constitution v6.0.1)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Defaults chosen (non-interactive run, no reviewer available to answer Q1–Q3)**:
- Q1 Depth → Standard, used as a formal gate before `$speckit-tasks`.
- Q2 Audience/timing → Reviewer of spec + plan, before task generation.
- Q3 Focus → five files: `general.md` (cross-cutting), `wiki-cli.md`, `error-ledger.md`, `eval-run.md`, `performance.md`. Must-have items: the six "Spec gaps for Clarify" in plan.md and the measured `wiki health` cold time (82.3 s).
- Owning step for a failing item: spec.md wording → Specify/Clarify; plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, or contracts → Plan.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Is the vault discovery order specified in the spec, or only in the plan (`--vault` > `OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH` > repo `.env` > `<repo>/wiki` > `~/.obsidian-wiki/config`)? The order decides which vault a clone lints. [Gap, Spec §FR-027, Research R6, Contract wiki-cli "Discovery"]
- [ ] CHK002 - Do FR-031 (layered help) and FR-032 (Examples block) apply to `scripts/luna-eval` and `scripts/error-ledger.py`, which FR-027 includes but which are not `wiki` subcommands? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-027, Spec §FR-031, Spec §FR-032]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is the structured result schema (required keys `status`, `vault`, `changed`, `counts`, `timing.duration_ms`, `next`) stated in the spec, or does FR-028/FR-038 leave it open? [Completeness, Spec §FR-038, Contract wiki-cli "Success output"]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are exit codes specified beyond "non-zero" for invalid input (contract uses 2), and for "findings present" vs "clean" vs "tool failure"? [Gap, Spec §FR-035, Contract wiki-cli "Errors"]
- [ ] CHK005 - Is "safe bookkeeping" (FR-028) enumerated per command, including whether `lint` may write the lint cache, identity index, and Vale vocabulary? [Clarity, Spec §FR-028, Plan "Spec gaps" #6]
- [ ] CHK006 - Does FR-029 define "repeated" (how many trajectory occurrences) and name the trajectories that are the evidence? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-029, Spec §FR-045]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 - Is "resource verb" command shape (FR-034) consistent with the subcommand names `lint`, `query`, `health`, `mutate`, `repair`, which are verbs or nouns without a resource? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-034, Contract wiki-cli "Shape"]
- [ ] CHK008 - Is "argument order MUST NOT matter" bounded for `lint fix` vs a page path literally named `fix`? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-034]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is "the next actionable target where one exists" defined for each command, including the value when none exists (`null`)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-038, Contract wiki-cli]
- [ ] CHK010 - Is "where to list valid values" (FR-035) specified per error case (unknown path vs unknown scope kind)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-035, Contract wiki-cli "Errors"]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 - FR-034 says `lint fix` MUST NOT be a positional `fix` token; research R6 and the contract keep the positional token as a working alias. Is that alias allowed by the spec? [Conflict, Spec §FR-034, Research R6, Contract wiki-cli "Shape"]
- [ ] CHK012 - Are FR-030–FR-038 consistent with feature 027's result contract (compact JSON default, `--pretty`, no fuzzy paths) that the spec keeps in force, notably the error JSON on stdout plus message on stderr? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions, Contract wiki-cli]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is rejecting `wiki/`-prefixed paths (no fuzzy paths) consistent with FR-027's goal that commands work "from any working directory", where a repo-relative path is natural? [Consistency, Spec §FR-027, Research R6]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is `--dry-run` required for `error-ledger` `migrate` in the spec (FR-037 "every mutating command")? The contract adds it; FR-036 lists only `append`/`drain`. [Consistency, Spec §FR-036, Spec §FR-037, Contract error-ledger]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 - Is "cold agent" in SC-010 defined (model, effort, context given, tasks per subcommand)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK016 - Is "invocation error" defined (non-zero exit from a CLI parse error only, or any retry with changed arguments)? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-010, Spec §US7]
- [ ] CHK017 - Does FR-039's "a regression test per rule class" name the rule classes, so coverage is countable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-039, Contract wiki-cli "Regression tests"]
- [ ] CHK018 - Is "0 additional changes" on rerun (SC-010) consistent with the status token: "already done" (US7-3), `already_done` (contract), or "zero changes" (FR-036)? [Consistency, Spec §US7, Spec §FR-036, Contract wiki-cli]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK019 - Are requirements defined for `--stdin` with empty input, duplicate paths, or a mix of valid and invalid paths (fail all vs partial)? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-033]
- [ ] CHK020 - Is dry-run output required to equal the real run's change set (so a dry run predicts the real run)? [Gap, Spec §FR-037, Quickstart V-16]
- [ ] CHK021 - Is behavior specified when the discovered vault does not exist or two discovery sources disagree (e.g. `.env` vs `<repo>/wiki`)? Is the chosen source reported? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-027, Contract wiki-cli "Discovery"]
- [ ] CHK022 - Is `--yes` specified only if a confirmation exists, and is the "no confirmation exists" state stated for each mutating command? [Clarity, Spec §FR-037, Contract wiki-cli "Mutation safety"]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`
- Markers: `[Gap]` missing requirement, `[Ambiguity]` unclear wording, `[Conflict]` two sources disagree, `[Assumption]` unvalidated premise. `Spec §` = spec.md; `Plan`, `Research R#`, `Data-model §#`, `Contract <name>`, `Quickstart V-##` = plan artifacts
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
